guideline_check: ESPEN 2021 kidney guideline recommendations quoted from the verified full text (Clin Nutr 2021;40(4):1644–1668); numbers, grades and consensus as printed.
nutrient_numbers: Composition per 1000 ml of Aminosteril Infant 6% from the Philippine product information supplied by Dr. W. G. M. Rivero (November 18, 2026). Every value is exactly 0.6 times the Aminoven Infant 10% SmPC value, which confirms the same formulation at 6%.

registrations.packaging: Type I Glass Bottle x 100 mL

summary: Aminosteril Infant 6% (Fresenius Kabi Austria GmbH) is a pediatric amino acid solution, registered in the Philippines as 100 ml glass bottles.
composition_notes: Lysine is given as L-lysine acetate, tyrosine as N-acetyl-L-tyrosine and cysteine as N-acetyl-L-cysteine; the equivalent free amino acid amounts are shown in the rows marked "=". The free amino acids add up to 60 g per liter (6%).
Without electrolytes and carbohydrates; contains taurine.
Same formulation as Aminoven Infant 10% (Fresenius Kabi), at 60% of its concentration.
dosing_limits: Continuous intravenous infusion through a central vein; maximum rate 0.1 g amino acids/kg/hour (Aminoven Infant SmPC 4.2). For the 6% solution, 1 g amino acids is 16.7 ml.

Maximum daily dose in g amino acids/kg: age 1 year 1.5 to 2.5 g/kg; 2 to 5 years 1.5 g/kg; 6 to 14 years 1.0 g/kg (Aminoven Infant SmPC 4.2; same in the South African PI). The Swiss text gives a preterm maximum of 2.5 g/kg/day. The SmPC's ml/kg figures are for the 10% solution and are not shown.
kidney_notes: Spanish SmPC and South African PI: patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency require an individualized dose; frequent monitoring includes urea nitrogen, ammonia, electrolytes, glucose and triglycerides (SmPC 4.4).
Swiss Fachinformation: renal insufficiency and unknown kidney function are listed as contraindications. National texts differ; follow the Philippine package insert.
Renal amino acid losses with amino acid imbalance can occur if the infusion is too rapid or in overdose (South African PI 4.8, 4.9).
guideline_heading: How it fits the ESPEN 2021 kidney nutrition guideline
guideline: ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 24: "No disease-specific enteral nor parenteral formula oriented for patients with reduced kidney function should be routinely utilized in every patient with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF in comparison to conventional formulas. Instead, their use is to be individualized (see recommendation 26)." Grade of recommendation B – Consensus (87.5% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 31: "Electrolytes abnormalities are common in patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF receiving KRT and shall be closely monitored." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement).
bottom_line: A pediatric amino acid solution, 60 g amino acids per liter with taurine and no electrolytes or carbohydrates; the ESPEN 2021 kidney guideline quoted here covers hospitalized adults. Dose it in g amino acids/kg, not in ml from the 10% product's tables.
withheld: Osmolarity, total nitrogen and energy of the 6% solution: not in the supplied product information (the Aminoven Infant 10% values do not apply). Check the bottle label.
